title: How small should a function be? - Robert C. Martin (Uncle Bob)
summary: Robert C. Martin: functions should be small, then smaller; extract until nothing more can be extracted, and the tiny named functions reveal the hidden classes.

assertions.quote: a function does one thing if you cannot meaningfully extract another function from it

verdicts.note: Smaller methods correlate with fewer defects up to a point, but studies find very small, deeply delegating methods hurt comprehension.

Interviewed developers cited 'implements a single task' as a positive for the most understandable method and 'too many responsibilities' as a negative for the least understandable one; five-developer opinion on four methods, no test of the 'extract until nothing further' rule.

assertions.quote: every large function is really a class with a bunch of little tiny functions inside it

verdicts.note: Extract Class from shared locals is a standard refactoring; 'every' overstates.

assertions.quote: the rule came about your function should fit on a screen well that meant that the functions had to be about 20 lines
